To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the building internal pressure response is governed by a dimensionless Helmholtz frequency ratio that represents a ratio of the Helmheltz resonance period to the turbulence period.
the governing equation for the internal pressure dynamics of a building is the same as that of Vickery.

the internal pressure response to a dominant opening in a building can be characterised by a number of dimension-less parameters, including the opening air slug inertial ratio, opening loss and inertia coefficient, and the turbulence integral length scale.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of building pressure induced through a single dominant opening.
the development of a predictive capability to determine internal pressure dynamics induced in a building by a dominant opening.
the internal pressure response of a building with a dominant opening, which is the dominant source of internal pressure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the internal pressure dynamic system of a building with a dominant opening is a complex system that requires further research and development to fully characterise and predict its behaviour under windstorm conditions for design purposes.

the internal pressure response at a dominant opening is governed by the opening air slug inertial ratio, the opening loss coefficient and the opening inertia parameter, which in turn are dependent on the turbulence spectrum, the building internal pressure response and the building geometry.

the internal pressure response of a full scale building with a dominant opening is dependent on the non dimensional parameters of the dominant opening, namely, the opening air-slug inertia ratio, the opening inertia coefficient and the opening loss coefficient; as well as the length ratio and the onset flow Mach numbers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the internal pressure response is governed by the Helmholt z resonance period, and that the internal pressure is a function of the Helmh olz frequency ratio, the opening air mass inertia ratio, and the opening loss coefficient.
the dominant opening internal pressure dynamic problem is a complex one, and it is necessary to be aware of the limitations of the various approaches to solving this problem.
, in the absence of a more complete theory, a volume distortion model-scale testing approach is recommended for the prediction of internal pressure response of buildings to windstorms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the internal pressure response of the full scale building is a function of the dominant opening, the building internal volume and the Helmholt z resonance period.

a full scale building internal pressure dynamic response is a function of a number of dimensionally independent parameters, and that a correct characterisation of the system is essential for correct estimation of internal pressure response and the loss/inertia coefficients.
a more rigorous approach to the formulation of the building internal pressure dynamics is needed, and that the non dimensional parameters that characterise this system should be used.
